Applying the quoted Rogers-Shephard stability theorem then gives the displayed Banach-Mazur bound. No computational certificate is required.

originality.rationale: A September 18 published result was inspected in full. Its stated theorem uses the full two-body Bezout coefficient beta(K), but the proof of its longest-chord and difference-body steps uses only the exact special tests A=K intersect (K-sv), B=[0,v]. Therefore the same proof already establishes a Banach-Mazur stability theorem under the restricted chord-test coefficient after replacing beta by that restricted supremum. Indeed its retained covariogram bound gives a stronger numerical lower bound than the simplified c^{-(n-1)} lambda_n(c)^n bound in the assigned record. The assigned theorem is thus mechanically contained in the earlier proof despite the weaker hypothesis not being named in its statement.
